evidence_items.explanation: Fodor and Pylyshyn connect systematic understanding of related sentences to structured representations and challenge connectionist accounts on that basis. This establishes the historical comparison, not an empirical verdict on 2022 systems.

evidence_items.publisher: Cognition; full-text reproduction hosted by Reinhard Blutner
evidence_items.locator: Introductory list of shortcomings of the Rumelhart–McClelland model
evidence_items.explanation: Pinker and Prince document failures in a neural language-learning model, including missing outputs and faulty linguistic generalizations. Their task was past-tense learning, so connecting these failures to modern comprehension errors is a comparison of broad categories.

Tests involving SCAN and RobustFill found continuing difficulty combining learned components in new ways, even with modified Transformers. This supports persistence of compositional generalization problems while explicitly acknowledging progress.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Aakanksha Chowdhery and colleagues, Google
evidence_items.locator: Section 6.3, Figure 9 and accompanying error analysis, page 20
evidence_items.explanation: The PaLM analysis identifies semantic-understanding errors, omitted reasoning steps, and anomalous outputs; Figure 9 shows that scaling corrected some but not all errors in each category. This supports persistent comprehension and reliability problems, while also providing evidence against unchanged error frequency.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Christo Kirov and Ryan Cotterell
evidence_items.locator: Section 6, Summary of Resolved and Outstanding Criticisms
evidence_items.explanation: This direct revisit reports substantial improvements on the original past-tense problem and resolution of many specific objections. It challenges a literal claim of unchanged deficiencies, but does not establish elimination of the broad failure categories across neural AI.

unresolved_gaps: There is no common measurement spanning the 1988 models and 2022 systems that establishes unchanged error rates, severity, or mechanisms.
The original articles do not operationalize Marcus's four labels as a single shared taxonomy.
Exact original publication days for the 1988 articles were not established; their available_at fields use conservative year-end bounds, not asserted publication days.
